facts.fact: Biometric Update, citing a ministry statement, says the government 'launched' the New Deal Technologique 'last year' (2025); it names no adopting act or body beyond the government.

The article says the strategy is structured as a Digital Master Plan of 12 priority programmes and about 50 key projects to 2034, to be funded by an estimated US$1.7 billion, with 2034 indicator targets such as 95 percent connectivity and 80 percent usage of digital services.

A digital governance steering committee, GouvNum, 'has been created' as part of the plan to oversee all digital transformation initiatives and is to be operational in the near future; no act is named.

The digital ministry recently convened stakeholders in Dakar on the Government Enterprise Architecture under the strategy, and in March (2026) the government launched a number of initiatives under it, including a digital government platform; the convening date is not given, so the publication date is used.

systems.owner: Government of Senegal (Ministry of Telecommunications and Digital Economy)
Ministry of Telecommunications and Digital Economy

note: Class national on the document's own description: four pillars (sovereignty, modernising public administration, digital economy, regional leadership) in a Digital Master Plan to 2034. Stated horizon 2034, no text linked, so no period fact. The article is inconsistent on the New Deal's label (a DPI strategy, a blueprint, a master plan). The article says the PM chairing GouvNum was 'then' Sonko, i.e. a change of PM since March 2026.
